input.description: Workout supplements: pre-workout, creatine, protein. We compete on price, not on marketing. Same formulations as the expensive brands for half the cost.

brief.statusReason: The advertiser clearly states they sell workout supplements, including pre-workout, creatine, and protein, with a focus on low cost.
brief.productSummary: Affordable workout supplements including protein, pre-workout, and creatine sold to fitness-conscious consumers at a budget price level.
assumptions: Assumed an average order value of approximately $30 based on budget-positioned protein and workout powders.
Assumed the primary purchase model is one-time transactional, though subscriptions may be offered.
Assumed a gender-neutral target audience interested in fitness and strength training.

persona.name: The Fitness Enthusiast
persona.description: Works out 4+ times a week, follows fitness creators, buys performance apparel and supplements. Brand-loyal to things that perform. Identity-adjacent purchasing.

persona.name: The Wellness Optimizer
persona.description: Tracks sleep, supplements, and workouts. Treats her body like a system to optimize. Willing to pay premiums for evidence-backed products.

reasons.label: low price sensitivity vs budget pricing

persona.name: The Value-Conscious Shopper
persona.description: Budget-aware but not low-end. Looks for deals, reads reviews, comparison shops. Responds well to bundles, first-order discounts, and clear value articulation.

reasons.label: high price sensitivity vs budget pricing

persona.name: The Gen Z Aesthete
persona.description: Highly visual, identity-expressive buyer. Discovers through TikTok and Instagram. Cares about brand voice, packaging, and whether the brand stands for something.

reasons.label: medium-high price sensitivity vs budget pricing

persona.name: The Busy Parent
persona.description: Dual-income household with kids. Time-poor, convenience-motivated. Buys in bulk, loves subscriptions, trusts brands that have been recommended by other parents.

persona.name: The Pet Parent
persona.description: Treats their pet as a family member. Reads ingredient labels on pet food. Will pay a premium for health and quality. Often owns multiple pets.

persona.name: The Affluent Classic
persona.description: Established career or retired, disposable income, values quality and longevity over trends. Shops less frequently but at higher AOVs. Loyal to brands she trusts.

reasons.label: low price sensitivity vs budget pricing

persona.name: The Sustainability Buyer
persona.description: Makes purchase decisions based on environmental and ethical footprint. Researches supply chains. Will pay more for genuinely sustainable options and is skeptical of greenwashing.

persona.name: The Convenience-First Millennial
persona.description: Urban, mid-to-high income, values speed and frictionlessness. Default to what's easy. Heavy subscription user. Low brand loyalty if another option is just as convenient.

persona.name: The Gifter
persona.description: Not a persistent persona so much as a mode: any shopper within 30 days of a gifting holiday or life event. Higher AOV, looking for 'impressive-looking' purchases. Very responsive to gift-wrap and gifting messaging.

reasons.label: low price sensitivity vs budget pricing

publisher.name: Daily Form
publisher.notes: Science-forward wellness. Audience skeptical of unsubstantiated health claims.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Fitness Enthusiast, The Wellness Optimizer

publishers.rationale: This science-forward wellness audience is highly analytical and skeptical of health claims, meaning your low-cost pre-workouts may face credibility hurdles.
publishers.concern: The highly skeptical, premium-leaning female demographic may reject budget performance supplements.

publisher.name: Movewell
publisher.notes: Fitness-engaged shoppers. Strong crossover with wellness and beauty.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Fitness Enthusiast, The Wellness Optimizer, The Value-Conscious Shopper
Audience responds to performance, health conscious

publishers.rationale: The highly fitness-engaged demographic shopping for activewear here represents an ideal customer base for performance-boosting pre-workouts and proteins.
publishers.concern: The high average order value and mid-high income tier might make budget-priced products less appealing.

publisher.name: Studiogrid
publisher.notes: Appointment-based booking. Users are actively spending on self-care and fitness.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Fitness Enthusiast, The Wellness Optimizer

publishers.rationale: Studiogrid caters to high-income users focused on premium boutique fitness classes and spas who are less likely to seek out budget-tier supplements.
publishers.concern: High-spending boutique fitness clients often prefer luxury or specialized supplement brands over value options.
publishers.exclusionReason: High-spending boutique fitness clients often prefer luxury or specialized supplement brands over value options.

publisher.name: Cloudfoot
publisher.notes: Tech-adjacent urban professionals. Comfort + sustainability messaging.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Fitness Enthusiast, The Wellness Optimizer

publishers.rationale: This audience prioritizes sustainability and premium urban comfort, showing little alignment with budget-oriented athletic performance products.
publishers.concern: The high-AOV, tech-adjacent customer base lacks direct fitness supplement purchasing signals.
publishers.exclusionReason: The high-AOV, tech-adjacent customer base lacks direct fitness supplement purchasing signals.

publisher.name: Pantrygood
publisher.notes: Values-driven shoppers. Responsive to clean-ingredient, sustainability, and wellness claims.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Wellness Optimizer, The Value-Conscious Shopper

publishers.rationale: Shoppers here prioritize organic, clean-label ingredients, which may clash with the formulation expectations of a budget workout supplement brand.
publishers.concern: The value-price positioning might signal low ingredient quality to natural grocery shoppers.
publishers.exclusionReason: The value-price positioning might signal low ingredient quality to natural grocery shoppers.

publisher.name: Pop & Sip
publisher.notes: Health-curious but indulgence-seeking. Strong overlap with wellness and premium grocery.

publishers.rationale: While health-curious, this audience is primarily looking for indulgent soda alternatives and gut health beverages rather than athletic performance supplements.
publishers.concern: Indulgence-seeking beverage shoppers have low intent for hardcore fitness products like creatine.
publishers.exclusionReason: Indulgence-seeking beverage shoppers have low intent for hardcore fitness products like creatine.

publisher.name: Stride & Stem
publisher.notes: Professional women. Sustainability and machine-washable claims resonate.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Fitness Enthusiast, The Value-Conscious Shopper

publisher.name: Strandlab
publisher.notes: Personalization-motivated audience. Quiz-based onboarding elsewhere.

publisher.name: Velvetline
publisher.notes: Gen Z and younger millennial. Minimalist aesthetic, identity-driven purchasing.

publishers.rationale: This publisher's focus on Gen Z makeup and minimalist skincare offers virtually no alignment with performance-driven fitness supplements.
publishers.concern: There is an extreme demographic and product mismatch with beauty-focused shoppers.
publishers.exclusionReason: There is an extreme demographic and product mismatch with beauty-focused shoppers.

publisher.name: Swiftcart
publisher.notes: High-frequency purchasers. Late-night traffic spike. Impulse-friendly.

publisher.name: Marlowe & Co.
publisher.notes: Older affluent women. Lower impulse but high AOV. Responds to quality messaging.

publisher.name: Everbody
publisher.notes: Inclusive sizing across the full range. Audience values representation and fit-focused messaging.

publisher.name: Pawline

publishers.exclusionReason: No overlap with your category or likely buyers

publisher.name: Kitchenly
publisher.notes: Family and couples households. Convenience-motivated but food-interested.

publisher.name: Linden Park
publisher.notes: Highest-AOV apparel publisher in the catalog. Conservative brand sensibility.

publishers.exclusionReason: No overlap with your category or likely buyers

plan.reviewNote: The current publisher landscape heavily skews toward premium wellness and beauty; we must prioritize Movewell and other activewear communities to find performance-focused consumers. Because many of these platforms feature high-income audiences, messaging should focus on the quality and performance benefits of the ingredients to overcome any budget pricing stigma.

bidding.rationale: Start on CPM bids for 14 days to buy reach and collect conversion data (there is no history yet), then switch to a target CPA once each publisher has ~30 conversions.

creativeRotation.strategy: Even rotation for 14 days, then shift weight to the best CTR per publisher.

assumptions: No budget given: assumed $10,000 for a 30-day test.
CPMs are estimated from each audience's income tier (+15% for audiences under 5M monthly impressions); real prices come from the auction.
One-time purchase: target CPA = 30% of order value as a margin-safe default.
No publisher gets more than 25% of its monthly impressions, so no single audience is saturated.
Assumed an average order value of approximately $30 based on budget-positioned protein and workout powders.
Assumed the primary purchase model is one-time transactional, though subscriptions may be offered.
Assumed a gender-neutral target audience interested in fitness and strength training.

output.understanding: The advertiser sells high-quality workout supplements like pre-workout, creatine, and protein directly to value-conscious fitness enthusiasts at half the price of major brands by focusing on identical formulations rather than expensive marketing.

publishers.rationale: Daily Form reaches a science-forward, analytical wellness audience that is highly skeptical of health claims and will appreciate exact ingredient formulation comparisons and transparency at a lower price point.
Movewell has a highly fitness-engaged shopper base with a strong crossover into wellness and health products, making it an ideal audience for active workout supplements.
Pop & Sip features health-curious and wellness-oriented buyers who actively purchase functional consumables, aligning well with clean-label, value-focused daily nutrition.

excluded.reason: Swiftcart focuses on instant convenience and grocery delivery with broad demographics, which is less targeted than dedicated fitness and wellness audiences.
Studiogrid caters to high-income fitness class attendees who are less price-sensitive and may not align well with a budget-friendly, minimalist-marketing value proposition.
Marlowe & Co. targets older, affluent women focused on classic fashion rather than active fitness and supplement consumers.
Linden Park targets a highly affluent, older female demographic shopping for luxury apparel, matching poorly with budget workout supplements.
Everbody is an apparel publisher focused on inclusive sizing and workwear rather than active fitness or workout nutrition.
Pawline is a pet-focused publisher with no relevance to human workout and fitness supplements.
Pantrygood caters to high-income organic grocery shoppers who prioritize wellness lifestyle branding over pure utility-and-price formulation arguments.
Ruffco is a pet food and supplies publisher with no relevance to athletic supplements.
Heartfoot focuses on basic apparel and gifting rather than active nutrition or fitness enthusiasts.
Northbed is a home textiles and bedding brand with no target audience alignment for sports nutrition.
Velvetline targets Gen Z and young millennials looking for aesthetic-forward beauty and skincare rather than athletic workout supplements.
Hearthstone Goods is focused on kitchenware and non-toxic home products, which is irrelevant to sports nutrition.
Kitchenly reaches meal-kit subscribers looking for family convenience rather than individual athletic performance supplementation.
Stride & Stem is an apparel publisher focused on women's sustainable footwear, which does not match sports nutrition.
Cloudfoot is an apparel brand focused on urban comfort shoes, making it less direct for performance supplement targeting than dedicated wellness/fitness properties.
Tailcrate is a subscription service for dog toys and treats with no alignment to human fitness supplements.
Strandlab is a personalized hair care DTC platform that does not align with price-conscious sports nutrition.

output.bidStrategy: Employ a cost-per-acquisition (CPA) target bidding strategy focused on direct-response conversions. Highlighting price and ingredient parity in the creative will yield high click-through and conversion rates among value-conscious fitness shoppers.
